Synopsis:
GD if the Dark Urge has murdered a companion after failing to kill Isobel.

Cluster Contexts:
- CAMP_GD_SparedIsobel_AfterMurder.json: The scene follows a Dark Urge playthrough in which, after failing to kill Isobel, the player has just murdered a companion — the corpse lies before them and other party members are approaching at night, roused by laughter and the sound of knife on bone. Off‑screen the PC is a Bhaalspawn haunted by violent compulsions and restless behavior; some companions (Astarion in other contexts, here Karlach) already suspect or have been directly endangered by the PC’s urges. The arriving companions react with fury, disbelief, or attempts to explain/mitigate (the PC may plead self‑defense, blame outside influence, feign accident, or revel in the deed). In other possible branches this confrontation can occur amid the Murder Tribunal beneath Baldur’s Gate, where the court’s demand for bloody proof and any prior killings of Bhaal‑kin shape how NPCs judge or threaten the player.
- CAMP_DarkUrge_SparedIsobel_SD.json: You wake in a bed after failing to kill Isobel; your grotesque, ever‑loyal Butler Sceleritas Fel appears at your bedside and taunts and cajoles you into giving in to the Dark Urge. The Butler openly urges you to murder whichever companion currently has your highest approval (or your romantic partner), even suggesting a staged confession and reminding you that he will be replaced if you kill him — and that kills help secure your “tithe” or inheritance. Off‑screen the player has been drugged/drowsy and at times unconscious or restrained, with companions nearby watching and pleading while the Urge claws at your hands. Separate Moonrise/Colony context notes (guards on high alert, mind‑melds for tadpoles, recent Execution/Audience events) may influence how others react afterward, and the scene explicitly excludes certain characters from being valid targets.
- MOO_Assault_DarkUrgeButlerReminder_AOM.json: The player has never spoken to Isobel before starting the assault on Moonrise. The Butler appears in front of the player on the bridge to Moonrise to remind the Dark Urge player that they must kill Isobel if they want to please Bhaal.
- CAMP_DarkUrge_Bloodwedding_SD_Nested_InWorld.json: The scene takes place inside the Bhaal temple where the Dark Urge protagonist and Orin the Red confront one another beneath a looming idol of Bhaal; a disembodied “butler”/temple voice (Sceleritas/Bhaal’s butler) narrates and reveals truths the player’s memory obscures. Off‑screen events leading here include Orin’s prior provocations in the city (and her role as a Bhaal Chosen) and the player’s brutal past killings — if the player followed the Embracing track, spectres of those victims appear in the vision. Only one of the two (either Orin or the player) will assume the Slayer form here; in most non‑Dark‑Urge playthroughs Orin transforms and combat follows, while if the Dark Urge player becomes the Slayer the scene branches into an immediate post‑transformation exchange (often Jaheira speaking about the Slayer, if she’s present). The butler’s voice frames the encounter as a family reunion and presses the player to confront their heritage and/or destroy their kin.
- CAMP_DarkUrge_Bloodwedding_SD.json: The scene is a waking vision inside the Bhaal temple: the Dark Urge and Orin face one another beneath a glowing Bhaal icon while Sceleritas Fel — Bhaal’s butler/door‑guardian — narrates as a disembodied voice rather than appearing in person. The Butler frames the player as a spawn of Bhaal, dredging up memories of murder and urging that only one Chosen may inherit the Slayer birthright, pressing the player to slay the “sister” before them. If the player followed the Embracing track, the vision includes spectres of past victims; otherwise it still presents vivid recollections and Bhaal’s claim. Only one character will assume the Slayer form here, and if the Dark Urge becomes the Slayer the cutscene should immediately transition into the companion reaction/dialogue (e.g., Jaheira) afterward. Orin’s taunts reflect an established, antagonistic rivalry tied to earlier city events and the wider plot.

context: You are playing a Dark Urge save in which the PC — a Bhaalspawn haunted by violent compulsions and prodding from a disembodied Butler figure — recently failed to kill Isobel and has just murdered a companion; the corpse lies before them at night. Other party members (here, notably Karlach) have been roused by the PC’s laughter and the sound of blade on bone and are approaching in fury, disbelief, or to try to restrain or explain away the act. The Butler is not present to celebrate in this moment, but his prior urging and the PC’s murderous history inform how others judge or accuse the PC. In dialogue the PC can react several ways consistent with the scene — plead self‑defense, blame outside influences (the Absolute), feign accident, or openly revel in the killing — and companions will respond accordingly.
